a03611fe03f6b324ddfe7a0149a54ca48536fd51.content:
{
"Water Heater": "An appliance that heats water for domestic use, typically delivering hot water to faucets, showers, and appliances in a household.",
"Tank Water Heater": "A type of water heater that stores and heats a reservoir of water inside an insulated tank, typically lasting ten to fifteen years with proper maintenance.",
"Gas Water Heater": "A tank water heater that uses a gas burner to heat the water inside the tank.",
"Electric Water Heater": "A tank water heater that uses electric heating elements submerged in the tank to heat the water.",
"Burner": "The gas-fired component of a gas water heater that produces heat beneath the tank to warm the water inside.",
"Heating Element": "An electrical component inside an electric water heater that converts electricity into heat to warm the surrounding water.",
"Upper Heating Element": "The heating element located in the upper portion of an electric water heater's tank, controlled by the upper thermostat.",
"Lower Heating Element": "The heating element located in the lower portion of an electric water heater's tank, controlled by the lower thermostat.",
"Tank": "The insulated steel vessel of a water heater that stores and holds heated water until it is drawn for use.",
"Tank Flush": "A maintenance procedure in which water is drained from the tank to remove accumulated sediment from the bottom.",
"Sediment": "Mineral deposits that settle at the bottom of a water heater tank, insulating the water from the heat source and reducing efficiency.",
"Hard Water": "Water containing high concentrations of dissolved minerals such as calcium and magnesium, which contribute to sediment and scale buildup.",
"Relief Valve": "A safety valve on a water heater that automatically opens to release water when temperature or pressure inside the tank becomes excessive.",
"Discharge Pipe": "A pipe attached to the relief valve that directs released water safely away from the valve outlet.",
"Anode Rod": "A sacrificial metal rod inserted into the tank that corrodes preferentially to protect the steel tank from rusting.",
"Magnesium Anode Rod": "An anode rod made of magnesium, commonly used for its strong sacrificial corrosion protection in water heater tanks.",
"Aluminum Anode Rod": "An anode rod made of aluminum, used as an alternative to magnesium especially in areas with hard water.",
"Core Wire": "The steel wire running through the center of an anode rod, which becomes exposed as the sacrificial metal corrodes away.",
"Calcium Buildup": "A hard, chalky deposit of calcium carbonate that forms on anode rods and other water heater components due to hard water.",
"Thermostat": "A control device that senses water temperature and regulates the burner or heating element to maintain the set temperature.",
"Upper Thermostat": "The thermostat controlling the upper heating element in an electric water heater, located behind an access panel.",
"Lower Thermostat": "The thermostat controlling the lower heating element in an electric water heater, located behind an access panel.",
"Access Panel": "A removable cover on the side of an electric water heater that provides access to the thermostat and heating element.",
"Temperature Setting": "The target water temperature configured on a water heater's thermostat, typically recommended at 120°F for safety and efficiency.",
"Standby Heat Loss": "The heat energy lost from a water heater's tank to the surrounding environment while the water sits idle and heated.",
"Gas Control": "The valve assembly on a gas water heater that regulates gas flow to the burner and includes settings such as 'pilot' and 'on'.",
"Pilot Setting": "A position on the gas control that keeps the pilot light lit but disables the main burner, used during maintenance.",
"Breaker": "An electrical circuit breaker that supplies power to an electric water heater and must be switched off before servicing.",
"Cold Water Supply Valve": "The shut-off valve on the cold water inlet line that stops incoming water flow to the water heater during maintenance.",
"Drain Valve": "A valve located near the bottom of the tank used to drain water and sediment during a tank flush.",
"Garden Hose": "A flexible hose attached to the drain valve to direct water from the tank to a floor drain or outside during flushing.",
"Floor Drain": "A drain in the floor used to receive water discharged from a water heater during flushing or maintenance.",
"Hot Water Faucet": "A household faucet opened during tank flushing to allow air into the plumbing system so water can drain or fill properly.",
"Bucket": "A container placed beneath the discharge pipe during a relief valve test to catch the water released from the valve.",
"Socket": "A tool fitting, typically 1-1/16 inch for anode rods, used with a wrench or breaker bar to loosen the rod from the tank.",
"Breaker Bar": "A long non-ratcheting handle used with a socket to apply high torque for loosening tightly secured fasteners such as anode rods.",
"Plumber's Tape": "A thin PTFE tape wrapped around threaded fittings to create a watertight seal when reinstalling components like the anode rod.",
"Rating Plate": "A label affixed to the side of a water heater listing its specifications, including tank capacity, recovery rate, and energy factor.",
"Tank Capacity": "The volume of water, measured in gallons, that a water heater's tank can hold at one time.",
"Recovery Rate": "The amount of water a water heater can heat to a specified temperature rise within one hour.",
"Energy Factor": "A rating that measures the overall energy efficiency of a water heater based on heating, standby losses, and cycling losses.",
"Scald Burn": "A serious skin injury caused by contact with hot water, which can occur within seconds at temperatures above 125°F.",
"Yearly Maintenance Routine": "An annual sequence of inspection and service tasks—including tank flush, relief valve test, anode rod inspection, and thermostat check—that extends water heater lifespan.",
"Relief Valve Test": "An annual check in which the relief valve's lever is lifted to verify that water discharges properly and the valve reseals without dripping.",
"Anode Rod Inspection": "A periodic examination of the anode rod, typically every two to three years, to determine if corrosion or calcium buildup requires replacement.",
"Household": "A group of people, typically a family, residing together in a home and consuming hot water from a shared water heater."
}
